title: Inference tactical handoff - Jun 02 2027
content:
Meeting: Inference tactical handoff
Date: 2027-06-02 10:00 PT (hybrid)
Chair: Sofia Martinez
Duration: 60m
Location: Zoom + Office 4B
Attendees: Sofia Martinez, Rahul Desai, Mei Wong, Carlos Rivera, Aisha Khan, Tom O'Neill, Priya Patel (+ async notes from infra team)

TL;DR:
- Short ops cadence to align runtime, SRE, observability, and product for the upcoming model + quantization rollout.
- Canary phase starts Wed 2027-06-09; target metrics and rollback triggers agreed.
- Two high-priority blockers: (1) KV cache eviction race on burst traffic; (2) Prom exporter missing token-level labels for new batching layer. Both assigned.

Agenda:
1) Quick metrics snapshot (Rahul)
2) Canary plan & gating criteria (Mei + Product)
3) Blockers and mitigations (All)
4) Downstream communication and consumer impact (Carlos)
5) Actions and owners (Sofia)

1) Quick metrics snapshot (Rahul)
- p50/p95 generation latency (hosted): 32ms / 184ms (baseline)
- steady-state token/sec per GPU: 7.9k tokens/sec (mixed A100/RTX pools)
- cache hit rate (prefix KV): 18% overall, but 42% on long-tail enterprise routes
- 24h error budget burn: 0.9% (within SLO but margin is thin given upcoming rollout)
- Notes: Observed small latency spike on 2027-05-30 13:15 UTC correlated with large batched rerank requests from a partner dev environment.

2) Canary plan & gating criteria (Mei + Product)
- Canary window: 2027-06-09 -> 2027-06-16, stepwise traffic ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30%
- Target metrics to validate each step:
  - p95 <= baseline + 20%
  - error rate delta <= 0.3 percentage points
  - token-level quality regression (prod eval set) <= 1.5% degradation on BLEU-like proxy
- Canary tooling: use canary-routing in runtime (route tag = canary-v2), enable extra traces and sampling at 10x for canary requests.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 breach for 10m or error rate spike > threshold or quality regression on the eval job (JIRA-INF-1499).
- Product concerns: A/B signals for paid customers must not be exposed; enforce route-level ACLs.

3) Blockers and mitigations (All)
- KV cache eviction race (priority P0)
  - Symptom: during short burst ramps, KV get/set can collide causing degraded hit rate and occasional duplicated token generation for a subset of requests. Repro on dev by replaying burst scenario.
  - Owner: Priya Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
  - Proposed fix: short-term patch to add CAS on cache writes; medium-term: refactor to per-tenant shard locks.
  - ETA: patch ready by 2027-06-06, test through replay infra, deploy canary patch 2027-06-07.

- Prom exporter missing token labels (priority P1)
  - Symptom: token-level telemetry from new batching layer lacks model_version and prompt_type labels, which prevents slice analysis during canary.
  - Owner: Tom O'Neill (observability)
  - Action: add labels to exporter and backfill partial metrics via trace sampling. PR #762 linked. Target merge 2027-06-05.

- Dedicated pool autoscaler flapping on small tenants
  - Symptom: min_replicas tuning causing repeated scale-up/down during burst windows.
  - Owner: Carlos Rivera (dedicated)
  - Mitigation: increase stabilization window to 90s for affected pools and apply smoothing policy. Change to be tested on staging by 2027-06-04.

4) Downstream communication and consumer impact (Carlos)
- Customer-facing note draft: short maintenance window messaging for canary start; ensure customers on dedicated/private are alerted if they rely on default model pins.
- Action: Carlos to publish a concise note to customers flagged as "sensitive-latency" by 2027-06-07. Template in linked_confluence page.
- Internal comms: post runbook and checklist to #serving-ops 24h before canary ramp. Include contact roster for on-call SRE.

5) Decisions made
- Proceed with canary as scheduled (2027-06-09) provided both P0 and P1 patches land on staging and pass replay tests.
- Sampling: increase request trace sampling to 10% for canary bucket to accelerate quality signal.
- No A/B feature exposure to end-users; all canary traffic must be hidden behind internal route keys.

6) Action items (owner -> due)
- Priya Patel -> prepare KV CAS patch + unit tests -> 2027-06-06
- Tom O'Neill -> merge exporter labels PR (#762) + smoke dashboards -> 2027-06-05
- Rahul Desai -> rehearse burst replay on canary infra and produce replay report -> 2027-06-07
- Carlos Rivera -> draft customer note + internal comms checklist -> 2027-06-07
- Mei Wong -> finalize canary rollout script and gating automation -> 2027-06-08
- Sofia Martinez -> run final gating review meeting on 2027-06-08 09:00 PT -> 2027-06-08

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should we enable quantized-int8 path for the canary or wait until post-canary? (ops leaning to postpone until post-canary due to observability gaps)
- Need decision on rolling timeout for slow requests > 30s and if we should tune circuit-breaker thresholds per route. (SRE follow-up)

Appendix / Useful links:
- Canary playbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Inference+Canary+Playbook
- Replay infra runbooks: https://github.com/redwood-infra/replay-runbooks
- Related Jira: JIRA-INF-1423 (burst-pattern replay), JIRA-INF-1499 (canary quality eval)
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/762 (exporter labels)

Notes to self / informal:
- Remember to ping legal for any customer note that mentions SLA windows.
- Mei: bring snacks next time for onsite folks.

Next sync:
- Final gating review: 2027-06-08 09:00 PT (mandatory for canary owners).
- Post-canary retrospective: 2027-06-17 10:00 PT.

End of notes.
